title: St. Egbert Music Ministry
text:
St. Egbert’s prides itself on its vibrant music ministry that offers something for everyone. Music for weekend liturgies currently includes:

Saturday 5:00 pm: cantor with guitar
Sunday 8:00 am: cantor with organ or piano
Sunday 9:30 am: Spanish Mass with Hispanic choir and band
Sunday 11:00 am: cantor and choir with organ or piano

Do you like to sing or play an instrument? Do you appreciate good liturgical music and want to help grow St. Egbert’s music ministry into the best in the region? Do you want to double your prayer without doubling your words?






Scan me to sign up!




Opportunities for involvement are listed below. Interested in joining? Scan the QR code to let us know your interest and contact info or speak to Matt, our music coordinator.

Adult Choir
The adult choir sings primarily at the 11 am Mass on Sundays. Rehearsals are Wednesdays 7:00-8:00 pm in the church from Labor Day through Pentecost.
Anyone 18 and older is welcome to join. The ability to read music is helpful but not required. Family of choir members are most welcome to join us in the choir area as well.
As we grow in numbers, we will begin (re-)introducting choir anthems and four-part harmony to further enhance our music and liturgies.







Cantors
Cantors lead the congregation in song at all liturgies. Any strong and confident singer (or anyone interested in becoming a strong and confident singer, which happens organically with practice) is welcome to become a cantor. Training will be provided. Cantor rehearsals take place on the first Tuesday of the month from 7:00-8:00 pm year-round in the church


Liturgical Ensemble
The liturgical ensemble is composed of adults, high school, and capable middle school instrumentalists. The ensemble enhances the 11:00 am liturgy on special occasions throughout the year, generally once a month. These include, but are not limited to:

Christmas (December)
Confirmation (usually February)
Last Sunday in Ordinary Time before Lent (February or early March)
Easter (March or April)
Pentecost (May or June)
Solemnity of Christ the King (November)

String, brass, and woodwind instruments are welcome. Rehearsals are Tuesdays 7:00-8:00 pm in the church from Labor Day through Pentecost.


Accompanists
Organists and/or pianists are needed to serve as substitute accompanists throughout the year, as well as for funerals and occasional weddings.


Singers and instrumentalists
Aside from the rehearsed choir, anyone who enjoys singing is welcome to join us in the choir area at whatever Mass you attend to sing with us. Similarly, anyone interested in playing an instrument more regularly than the liturgical ensemble is also welcome to participate any weekend. Instrumentalists are asked to consult with the music director to coordinate getting music, either day-of or in advance.

title: Weddings at St. Egbert’s
text:
Congratulations on your big day! We offer many prayers for you for a lifetime of blessings and happiness.
For Catholics, a wedding is a liturgical celebration of the sacrament of Holy Matrimony (marriage), a sacrifice of two people becoming one in God. What is liturgy, you ask? Liturgy is at the heart of what the church does: it is our public worship of God, our creator. And what is worship? It is giving thanks and honor to God that is due to him for all he has given to us. It is our expression of honor, acknowledgement, and respect to and for God because he is greater than us in all ways.
Everything about the wedding liturgy, including the music, is about your worship of God and God alone. For this reason, the Church prohibits popular music of any kind within the liturgy. Liturgical music must be deliberate, appropriate, and “correspond to the spirit of the liturgical celebration itself” (Instruction on Music in the Liturgy, 9). To help you plan your worship of God at your wedding liturgy, we provide instructions and suitable music options below. Click on the title of any piece to listen to a sample recording.
We encourage you to use this web form to submit your choices. For questions or assistance, or if you would prefer to have us select your music for you, please reach out to Matt Grossi, music director and organist, at mgrossi@stegbert.org.

title: Weddings at St. Egbert’s
text:
Other Logistics
Wedding stipends for trained musicians are due at the start of ceremony:

Organist: $200 (includes music coordination and playing the ceremony)
Cantor: $150
Music rehearsal(s): $50 each

Guest musicians, both cantors and instrumentalists, will be considered on a case-by-case basis, at the discretion of the music director and/or pastor. If you would like to include guest musicians, please indicate this in the form on the last question. All guest musicians must be both comfortable and experienced with the Catholic liturgy and will need to attend a music rehearsal with any parish musicians before the day of the wedding. (Note that this rehearsal is not the same as, nor can it occur at the same time as, the actual wedding rehearsal.) The music director may request an additional rehearsal if necessary to ensure the liturgy will flow smoothly. While every attempt will be made to welcome and include guest musicians, the music director and pastor both reserve the right to exclude anyone deemed too uncomfortable with the liturgy or incapable of meeting the standards of a liturgical musician.
Requests for liturgical music not in the parish hymnal will be considered on a case-by-case basis, at the discretion of the music director. If you would like a particular piece to be considered, please provide the name, composer, and, if possible, a link to a YouTube video in the form on the last question. If the piece is deemed appropriate but St. Egbert Church does not have a license to use it, the couple is responsible for purchasing the sheet music and rights to perform in advance of the wedding. (These usually go hand-in-hand, and costs are typically nominal, but be sure to verify when purchasing.) Keep in mind that musicians (accompanist and cantor) may need ample time to practice unfamiliar pieces, so please plan accordingly.


“The marriage covenant, by which a man and a woman form with each other an intimate communion of life and love, has been founded and endowed with its own special laws by the Creator.” (On the Church in the Modern World, 48)

title: St. Egbert Organ Replacement Project
text:
The organ at St. Egbert’s is now more than 30 years old, making it vulnerable to part failures and ongoing repairs. Its sound sampling technology is outdated and uninspiring by modern standards, and the instrument itself is undersized for the church and the parish’s music ministry program. The parish should begin proactively planning and raising money to replace it within the next few years, aiming to do so before it stops working to a degree that it is unfeasible to repair. Estimated project cost for 2026 is $212,000 (all inclusive), with prices increasing roughly 10-15% each year—another reason to act sooner rather than later.
The recommended target organ for St. Egbert Church is an Allen III/58 three-manual instrument at an estimated price of $211,578 (cost breakdown below).
This proposal details why a new organ is needed, identifies and justifies the ideal replacement instrument, and provides an analysis of alternatives. Templated fundraising materials—an informational pamphlet and a fundraising pledge page—are appended for consideration as well.



The Allen III/58 three-manual organ features “APEX II Technology [offering] the pinnacle of organ design for the 21st century. Combining the most advanced tone generation technology, unique features, build quality and product longevity.” (Allen Organ)

title: Mass of St. Dymphna
text:
Fr. Ryszard has asked us to learn and starting singing the Mass of St. Dymphna. We will begin introducing these Mass parts to the congregation starting Lent 2026, which begins on Wednesday, February 18.
Audio samples are below. Download a copy of the cantor sheet here.
We will start by introducing the Holy, Memorial Acclamation, and Great Amen. We will then add the Lamb of God and, after Lent, the Gloria.






ImportantCantors and choir members: Please start learning these now!



As vocal leaders, you will need to comfortably lead these parts until the congregation learns them well enough to sing. We will learn them together at choir and cantor rehearsals between now and then. (Note that we will sing all of them faster than performed here.)
